title: 2.4 Angles of elevation and depression

q.Q2: Q2. From a point 50 m from the foot of a building, the angle of elevation of the top is 32°. Find the height of the building. (tan 32° = 0.6249)
q.Q3: Q3. A student with eyes 1.5 m above the ground measures the elevation of a flagpole top. Why must 1.5 m be added to the calculated height?

q.Q4: Q4. From the top of a lighthouse 45 m high, the angle of depression of a ship is 18°. How far is the ship from the foot of the lighthouse? (tan 18° = 0.3249)

q.Q5: Q5. A girl sees the top of a tower at an angle of elevation of 30°. After walking 40 m towards it, the angle is 60°. Find the height of the tower.
q.Q6: Q6. Why is the angle of elevation larger when you are nearer the tower?

q.Q7: Q7. Using a clinometer, a student 1.6 m tall stands 25 m from a flagpole and measures an angle of elevation of 28°. Find the height of the flagpole. (tan 28° = 0.5317)

q.Exit ticket: Exit ticket. Why is the angle of elevation from A to B equal to the angle of depression from B to A?
